nodes.name: Access Control & Admin Operations
nodes.purpose: Manage who can do what inside the platform — invitations, permission grants, role changes, and org lifecycle management — so that every permission is precise and every action is auditable.
nodes.ux_intent: Setting up a new team member or changing someone's role feels like updating a contact card — two taps, done, no IT ticket needed.
nodes.vertical_notes: In caregiving agencies, role boundaries are especially important — a dispatcher should never be able to approve credentials; only a senior admin should. For cleaning, a team leader may be an elevated role with partial admin rights.

nodes.name: Invitations
nodes.purpose: Allow admins to bring new workers, clients, or staff into the platform by generating and sending invite links that pre-configure their role.
nodes.ux_intent: Inviting someone is as easy as sending a WhatsApp link — the invitee taps it, sees a friendly onboarding flow, and is set up in minutes.

nodes.name: Create Invite Link
nodes.purpose: Generate a cryptographically secure invite token that pre-configures the recipient's role and org membership when they onboard.
nodes.ux_intent: Admin fills out a simple form: 'Who are you inviting?' and 'What role?' — the platform generates a shareable link instantly.
nodes.vertical_notes: Worker invites go to nannies/cleaners applying to join. Staff invites go to dispatchers or supervisors.

nodes.name: Send Invite Notification
nodes.purpose: Deliver the invite link to the recipient via email or SMS with a clear call-to-action.
nodes.ux_intent: The invite email reads like a personal note from the agency: 'Hi Jane — we'd love you to join our nanny team. Click here to get started.'
nodes.vertical_notes: Worker invites should feel warm and encouraging, not transactional.

nodes.name: Accept Invite
nodes.purpose: Process an invitee clicking their invite link — validate the token, and either create a new account or link to their existing one, then attach the proposed OrgMembership.
nodes.ux_intent: Tapping the invite link opens a beautiful landing page: 'Welcome to [Agency Name]!' with a simple sign-up form — not a wall of fields.
nodes.vertical_notes: If the invitee already has an account in another org, their identity merges gracefully — they don't re-register.
nodes.case_integration: If the invitee is a worker, their OrgMembership seeds a Case Portfolio stub profile.

nodes.name: Revoke Invite
nodes.purpose: Invalidate an invite link before it is accepted — used when an admin sends one to the wrong person or changes their mind.
nodes.ux_intent: One-tap revocation with a 'This invite was revoked' message if the old link is clicked.

nodes.name: List Pending Invites
nodes.purpose: Show all outstanding invite links and their status so admins can track who has and hasn't accepted.
nodes.ux_intent: A clean table: 'Jane Smith — Nanny — Sent 2 days ago — Pending'. Admins can resend or revoke from the same view.

nodes.name: Roles & Permissions
nodes.purpose: Define and manage the permission sets for each role within an org (admin, dispatcher, team_leader, worker, client) — what each role can see and do.
nodes.ux_intent: Permissions feel like checking boxes: 'Can view client details: ✓'. No cryptic permission codes.
nodes.vertical_notes: Caregiving: dispatcher can reassign workers but cannot approve DBS checks — that's admin-only. Cleaning: team leader can assign jobs but not set billing rates.

nodes.name: Change Member Role
nodes.purpose: Promote or demote an OrgMembership to a different role, instantly updating their permission set.
nodes.ux_intent: A dropdown on a person's profile card: 'Role: [Worker ▾]' → changes take effect immediately with a toast confirmation.
nodes.vertical_notes: Promoting a senior nanny to 'team_leader' gives them access to the roster but not billing.

nodes.name: Check Permission
nodes.purpose: Evaluate whether the authenticated user's role grants them the requested action — used as a guard on every API endpoint.
nodes.ux_intent: Invisible to the user — they simply can't see or click things they're not allowed to do.

nodes.name: View Own Permissions
nodes.purpose: Let a member see exactly what actions they're permitted to take within the org — removing confusion about why certain features aren't available.
nodes.ux_intent: A simple 'Your permissions' page: 'You can ✓ View worker profiles / You cannot ✗ Change billing rates'.

nodes.name: Organisation Lifecycle
nodes.purpose: Manage the creation, configuration, and closure of an agency — the admin operations that exist at the org level rather than the member level.
nodes.ux_intent: Org setup feels like a guided wizard — 'Let's build your agency in 5 steps' — not a settings menu of despair.
nodes.vertical_notes: The initial org setup wizard is critical — it seeds the vertical (caregiving/cleaning), credential taxonomy, service types, and payment split before any worker is added.

nodes.name: Org Setup Wizard
nodes.purpose: Guide a brand-new admin through configuring their agency: vertical selection, credential taxonomy, service types, payment split, and first invite.
nodes.ux_intent: Feels like setting up a beautiful new app — friendly questions, clear progress bar, satisfying completion screen. 'Your agency is live!'
outputs: Org fully configured: credential types seeded, service types seeded, first admin membership created
nodes.vertical_notes: Wizard pre-seeds standard nanny credentials (DBS, First Aid, Paediatric First Aid) and standard service types (Daily Nanny, Live-in, Emergency Cover) if 'nanny' is selected. For cleaning: pre-seeds COSHH, DBS, regular domestic, deep clean, end-of-tenancy.
open_questions: Should the wizard be resumable if admin quits halfway through?

nodes.name: View Org Settings
nodes.purpose: Allow the admin to review and update top-level org settings (name, branding, contact info, vertical).
nodes.ux_intent: An intuitive settings page that feels like editing a company profile on LinkedIn — clear sections, inline edit.

nodes.name: Suspend Org
nodes.purpose: Temporarily disable the org — blocking new assignments, logins, and communications — during a platform review or non-payment.
nodes.ux_intent: Platform-level action, invisible to end users other than a 'Service temporarily unavailable' notice.

nodes.name: Close Org
nodes.purpose: Permanently wind down an org — settling final invoices, archiving records, and notifying all members.
nodes.ux_intent: A serious, deliberate action with clear confirmation ('This will permanently close your agency'). Not accessible from the main nav.
nodes.vertical_notes: Must handle outstanding invoices, active assignments (prompt to close them first), and worker holiday pay payouts.
open_questions: How long should data be retained after org closure?

nodes.name: Authentication
nodes.purpose: Manage all authentication flows — login, logout, password/OTP reset — for authenticated users, while allowing anonymous sessions for clients who haven't registered.
nodes.ux_intent: Logging in feels instant — phone OTP arrives in 3 seconds, you're in. No passwords to forget.
nodes.vertical_notes: Workers are primarily on mobile — phone OTP is the best auth method. Admins may prefer email + password.
nodes.case_integration: Supabase Auth (same as Case Portfolio) — enables seamless cross-platform SSO if the same phone number is used.

nodes.name: Login with Phone OTP
nodes.purpose: Authenticate a user by sending a one-time passcode to their phone number and verifying it.
nodes.ux_intent: One screen, one number input, one code input. Done. Feels like the smoothest possible gate.
nodes.case_integration: Shared Supabase Auth project — single identity across Case + Agency.

nodes.name: Login with Email + Password
nodes.purpose: Authenticate a user via email and password — primarily used by admin staff accessing from desktop.
nodes.ux_intent: Standard login with a clearly visible 'Forgot password?' link. No surprises.

nodes.name: Logout
nodes.purpose: Revoke the user's active session and clear all local auth state.
nodes.ux_intent: A clean, instant logout. User lands back on the welcome screen with a confirmation.
